h: How to win the room (or at least not lose badly)
p: A few tips go a long way at Immersive Gamebox. Wear trainers and comfortable clothes, because you'll be moving around more than you think. Leave big bags and coats somewhere sensible so they don't trip anyone up, and listen properly to the briefing at the start. The groups who talk to each other and split jobs, one on targets, one on puzzles, one keeping an eye on the timer, tend to do far better than those who all charge at the same wall.

Sessions run for a set length, so check what you're booking and allow a little time either side for arriving and catching your breath afterwards. Games rotate, so it's worth seeing what's on before you go and picking something that suits your group, whether that's a family-friendly theme or something a bit more intense for older players.

Stratford has changed massively since the 2012 Olympics, and there's lots more to explore once you're done. West Ham United play at the London Stadium on the Olympic Park, the Lee Valley VeloPark lets you see the famous velodrome, and Here East and Hackney Wick nearby have a creative, canal-side feel with independent cafes and bars.
For a breath of fresh air, the River Lea and its towpaths run through the park, so you can take a gentle stroll north or south. It makes a nice calm-down after the frantic energy of the gaming room.
